title: Microsoft Purview: per-policy coverage report for auto-labeling
summary: Hold: the licensing paragraph carries a client-side licence list across to service-side auto-labeling, although Microsoft now explicitly warns against doing so and directs administrators to its feature matrix. The report's navigation, PowerShell alternative, rollout information and 30-day window are supported.

claims.claim: The roadmap was modified at 2026-11-11T00:52:46.
Microsoft Purview Information Protection gains a per-policy auto-labeling coverage report.
claims.quote: For each enforced auto-labeling policy, admins can view how files processed during enforcement correlate to the latest simulation run.

claims.claim: View coverage appears in the policy list after a policy is turned on following simulation.
claims.quote: After an auto-labeling policy has been turned on following a simulation run, a new View coverage action will be available from the auto-labeling policy list.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: The report compares enforcement outcomes with the latest simulation.
claims.quote: The per-policy coverage report shows volumes of files that have been labeled or are not yet labeled, and whether those files were included in the last simulation snapshot.

claims.claim: The report shows labeled files, files still being processed and files with unsuccessful label application.
claims.quote:
The report provides a centralized view of files that were successfully labeled, files that are still being processed, and files that require attention.
Investigate files where label application was unsuccessful.

claims.claim: Microsoft's notice includes files no longer eligible because they were deleted or modified after simulation.
claims.quote: Identify files that remain pending, have not yet been processed, or are no longer eligible for labeling because they were deleted or modified after the simulation run.

claims.quote: **Observed files** | Files included in this report because they were found during simulation, enforcement, or both.

claims.claim: The report has a Labeled during enforcement area.
claims.quote: **Labeled during enforcement** | Files that had a label applied during enforcement.

claims.claim: The report has a Not labeled during enforcement area.
claims.quote: **Not labeled during enforcement** | Files that don't have a successful label application in this report.

claims.claim: The report has a Found in simulation area.
claims.quote: **Found in simulation** | Files that were found in the latest simulation run.

claims.claim: The report has a No simulation match found area.
claims.quote: **No simulation match found** | Files that weren't matched to the latest simulation run.

claims.claim: The report has a Pending area.
claims.quote: **Pending** | Files that don't have a final enforcement outcome yet.

claims.claim: The report has a Not yet attempted area.
claims.quote: **Not yet attempted** | Files that enforcement hasn't attempted to label yet.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost; Open questions
claims.claim: The feature page lists service-side auto-labeling as included with Microsoft 365 E5, E5 Compliance, E5 Information Protection & Governance and Azure Information Protection Premium P2 standalone.
claims.quote: Check the **Client and service-side automatic sensitivity labeling** entry in the feature matrix linked below. Client-only entitlements don't establish service-side entitlement.
claims.fix: Replace the service-side SKU sentence and licensing.notes SKU list with: "Microsoft's Purview service description lists Microsoft 365 E5 and Microsoft 365 E5 Information Protection and Governance among the subscriptions that include client and service-side automatic sensitivity labeling." Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/office365/servicedescriptions/microsoft-365-service-descriptions/microsoft-365-tenantlevel-services-licensing-guidance/microsoft-purview-service-description. The feature page now gives the old four-SKU list for client-side labeling only. Remove the standalone AIP P2 service-side entitlement implication, including 'or P2-tier' in the cost rationale and 'E5-tier licensing listed for auto-labeling' in the first open question; use 'published service-side auto-labeling licensing' instead.

claims.claim: E3 and Business Premium manual-labeling entitlement does not include automatic labeling.
claims.quote: **You have E3 or Business Premium.** Manual labeling entitlement doesn't include automatic labeling. Check the feature matrix for an eligible subscription or add-on for the labeling method you intend to use.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Licensing is marked unknown because entitlement specific to the coverage report has not been published.
claims.quote: Auto-labeling is gated by license, and the two surfaces (client-side and service-side) appear in different places in the portal.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to "included". Start licensing.notes with "The report is a view within licensed service-side auto-labeling; no separate report-specific licence or meter is documented as of November 2026." In Cost and licensing replace "The licence and any meter for the coverage report itself are not yet published" with "No separate licence or meter for the coverage report is documented as of November 2026". Keep only the corrected service-side entitlement statement specified in the licensing correction.
